items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: I did some gigs years ago, Warren Vache, Michael Hashim on saxophone, James Chirillo the guitarist, Chip Jackson on bass and Dennis Mackrel who was here with the Dizzy band.

ctx.x: Yeah. Steel fortitude for one. Yeah I’ve sort of gotten away from a lot of it. I think playing for a singer is kind of interesting for a pianist, or an arranger, but especially for a pianist. Because I’ve learned a lot of tunes over the years and in any key. So for pianists, if nothing else, just knowing the repertoire of the great American songs, plus being able

to play them in a lot of keys. And so for that it was fun. Obviously for some singers I like playing for and dealing with more than others. But I learned, again, I learned a lot. And also I like writing for singers. I haven’t done so much of that in a while. I did a record for Nnenna Freelon about three years ago called “Maiden Voyage” for Concord and we used different small groups. But generally, this wonderful singer, Jennifer Holliday, who did the original “Dream Girls” cast is a wonderful singer. We just did…
pianist plays better in that key kind of a thing. And I’ll say well look it, let’s try this a half a step lower, a half a step higher. And they say wow, it feels much better.
